post_copy:
Who has to be told before somebody changes the weather over the southern Kenai? The answer is not the borough underneath.

On August 23rd, 19 flares put about 374 grams of silver iodide into the clouds. Federal law takes a filing at least 10 days out. Rainmaker asked Alaska DNR first and got a letter of no objection. The borough found out from the press release.

The state reviewed it and found no violation. Alaska has no law of its own and no bill among this session's 856. The borough wrote the one rule it can enforce, ten questions about chemicals, flares and coordinates, on borough land only. None asks about the modeling that picks the cloud.

The ten items as the ordinance writes them, what the state found, and the blank in the form.

The hearing is October 20th. Who belongs on that address line before the next flight?

#CloudSeeding #KenaiPeninsula #AlaskaPolicy

slides.headline: EVERY NOTICE WENT UP. NONE CAME DOWN.
slides.body: 19 FLARES OVER THE SOUTHERN KENAI, AUGUST 23RD

slides.headline: Notice was given. It went up.
slides.body: Federal law bars anyone from changing the weather without filing a report, and the rule sets that filing at least 10 days before the activity begins. Rainmaker asked Alaska DNR first, and it answered with a letter of no objection.

slides.headline: The drones flew over state land.
slides.body: Because the flight was over state and not borough land, no borough permission was needed. The borough's own attorney put the limit in writing, that a second class borough has no authority to fully regulate this or the airspace.

slides.headline: 19 million gallons is a hundredth of an inch.
slides.body: Rainmaker flew 10 drone flights on August 23rd and its report puts the result at about 57 acre-feet, or roughly 19 million gallons, which works out to about 0.01 inches across the area. The state calls these modeled estimates, not water measured at the ground.

slides.headline: The borough's port was never drilled.
slides.body: Rainmaker's press release was the first notice the borough had that drones carrying weather modification payloads were operating inside it. The flight was over state land, so no borough permission was needed.

slides.headline: The borough wrote a form.
slides.body: Ten required items, on borough land only.

slides.headline: Ten questions. None about the model.
slides.body: The state's own letter says the company uses drones, atmospheric observations, weather radar and modeling to identify clouds and conditions suitable for seeding. Every one of the ten items asks about the payload, the pyrotechnics or the flight.

slides.headline: Everyone can ask. Almost nobody can act.
slides.body: Alaska has no framework specific to weather modification and no state permit is required for cloud seeding. This session carries 856 bills and not one of them is on the subject. Federal law takes a filing, not a permission.

slides.headline: One room. October 20th.
slides.body: The public hearing and final vote on the ordinance is October 20th, and if the Assembly enacts it, it takes effect immediately. Until then it is introduced and not law.

aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time.
Paste the first comment within 60 seconds of posting, so the sources are up before the first readers arrive.
Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. A dead first hour is rarely recovered.

If anyone reads this as an accusation, the correction is on slide 04: the state reviewed the flight and identified no violation and no adverse impact. The company also told the state that talking to officials beforehand would have been appropriate, which is worth saying in a reply. It was on slide 08 until the deck's last pass, where it was making the frame the longest read in the carousel.
The ordinance is INTRODUCED and NOT ENACTED. If a commenter says the borough has banned cloud seeding, that is wrong and slide 06 says so on its face.
The hearing is October 20th. This deck has a shelf life and it is best posted well before then.

A Kenai commenter will raise Rep. Sarah Vance within the first hour. She has DRAFTED a weather modification bill she would introduce if reelected, which is why slide 08 is accurate that none of this session's 856 bills is on the subject and why the reply is that a drafted bill is not a filed one. There is no bill number because there is no bill.
editor_notes_for_email: Shipped as an explicit UPDATE to No.42, declared on the cover. The caption room's winner was candidate B, QUESTION FIRST over ZOOM, and the critic's one fix was applied. That critic also caught a real defect in the DECK, not just the caption: slide 02 had asserted that Rainmaker filed its federal report, which no claim verifies. The slide now names the federal requirement rather than implying a completed filing, and the argument is better sourced for it.
